title: Collection of Quasi-kinematical 4D STEM Data with DigitalMicrograph
content: Acquiring maps of electron diffraction data with the popular 4D STEM technique enables several kinds of data analysis including strain mapping, differential phase contrast (DPC) imaging, and crystal orientation mapping. It has been reported that utilizing precession electron diffraction (PED) techniques to acquire quasi-kinematical diffraction data with fewer dynamical effects can improve the precision of electron diffraction studies [1]. This abstract introduces a strategy for acquiring quasi-kinematical 4D STEM diffraction data directly within DigitalMicrograph®. This allows microscopists to leverage the full speed, sensitivity, and dynamic range of their on-axis electron detector cameras without needing additional hardware beyond the requirements for acquiring 4D STEM data.
